description: Tissue classes of the atlas flow phantom (label id = index) and their 3 T properties. Rounded literature values; water compartment relaxation unless noted, the fat compartment (fraction ff of pd) uses the 'fat' row. chi: SI volume susceptibility in ppm. Native (no contrast) values; contrast agents are a separate relaxivity model.
sources: Stanisz GJ et al. T1, T2 relaxation and magnetization transfer in tissue at 3T. MRM 2005;54:507-512
de Bazelaire CMJ et al. MR imaging relaxation times of abdominal and pelvic tissues at 3.0 T. Radiology 2004;230:652-659
Bojorquez JZ et al. What are normal relaxation times of tissues at 3 T? MRI 2017;35:69-80
Zhao JM et al. Oxygenation and hematocrit dependence of transverse relaxation rates of blood at 3T. MRM 2007;58:592-597
Hamilton G et al. In vivo characterization of the liver fat 1H MR spectrum. NMR Biomed 2011;24:784-790
Schenck JF. The role of magnetic susceptibility in magnetic resonance imaging. Med Phys 1996;23:815-850

notes.fat: adipose: ff 0.9 of the proton density is fat (methylene peak, single-peak model; multi-peak spectrum per Hamilton 2011 later)
notes.bone_marrow: axial-skeleton red/yellow mix, ff ~0.45; trabecular bone shortens T2* and makes chi more diamagnetic
notes.lung: voxel-averaged parenchyma: tissue+blood fraction ~0.2, air 0.8 (chi = 0.8 x 0.36 + 0.2 x -9.05)
notes.blood: native blood, Hct 0.42; arterial Y 0.98, venous Y 0.70 (T2 / T2* and chi shift from deoxyhaemoglobin: dchi = 4 pi 0.27 ppm x Hct x (1 - Y))
